skill.name: zapier-workflows
skill.description: Manage Zapier MCP actions and webhook-triggered workflows while documenting reusable tool preferences, trigger phrases, and orchestration patterns.
skill.summary: Run and document reusable Zapier automations through MCP tools and webhooks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Sixty-three static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, expected Zapier endpoints, and standard Claude skill directories. One low-severity alert is confirmed because reset instructions redirect users to a different community repository. Semantic review found high-risk plaintext credential storage, unconfirmed automation execution, and persistent self-modification.

remediation.issue: Webhook URLs containing bearer capabilities are stored in plaintext skill files.
remediation.suggestion: Store secrets in an approved secret manager and keep only opaque references in skill files.

remediation.issue: The execution flow triggers side-effecting Zaps before presenting a confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Show the target, inputs, and expected actions, then require explicit approval before every webhook POST or mutating MCP call.

remediation.issue: User-provided workflow text can be persisted into instruction-adjacent reference files.
remediation.suggestion: Use a strict data schema, reject instruction-like content, and require review before writing persistent workflow records.

remediation.issue: Reset instructions reference a repository that differs from the audited marketplace source.
remediation.suggestion: Use the canonical source URL and pin reset instructions to a reviewed commit or release.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext Storage of Webhook Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The skill stores webhook URLs in reference files even though those URLs authorize Zap execution. File disclosure or accidental commits can expose automation access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly says webhook URLs contain authentication tokens and are stored in plaintext. This is a direct credential-handling design decision.

semantic_findings.title: Side-Effecting Automations Run Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The execution sequence triggers webhook Zaps or MCP tools before confirmation. Broad trigger words can start costly or externally visible workflows without a final approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The ordered workflow places execution before confirmation and includes direct webhook POSTs. No preview, allowlist, or approval gate is specified.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Self-Modification From Conversational Input
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to persist user-provided workflow text in instruction-adjacent files. Unvalidated content can influence later sessions and tool use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly requires self-editing and permanent pattern storage. It defines no schema validation or review boundary for persisted text.

content.value_statement: Zapier workflows are difficult to recall and coordinate across sessions. This skill documents preferred tools and helps execute approved MCP actions or webhook automations.
actual_capabilities: Documents named Zaps, trigger phrases, webhook details, timing, costs, and expected outputs.
Selects between webhook-triggered Zaps and direct MCP tool orchestration using documented decision rules.
Calls connected Zapier MCP tools for actions such as research, email, and Google Sheets updates.
Triggers documented multi-step Zaps through webhook POST requests.
Records approved tool preferences and reusable workflow sequences in reference files.
limitations: Requires a Zapier account and configured webhooks or MCP tools.
Cannot create or repair Zapier dashboard workflows without the required account access.
Stores webhook details in plaintext unless the user applies separate secret management.
Depends on the availability, permissions, and behavior of connected third-party services.

use_cases.title: Run Recurring Operations
use_cases.description: Match a named request to a documented multi-step Zap, present its effects, and trigger it after approval.

use_cases.title: Research and Record Findings
use_cases.description: Use documented research tools, summarize results, and save approved findings to a preferred Google Sheet.

use_cases.title: Track Sales Activity
use_cases.description: Coordinate approved lead enrichment and tracking actions through available Zapier MCP tools.

prompt_templates.title: Review Available Automations
prompt_templates.prompt: List my documented Zaps and explain which one best matches [goal]. Do not run anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants to understand available workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Record an Expense
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my documented Google Sheets preference to record [expense details]. Show the planned fields and request approval before writing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants a simple, controlled MCP action.

prompt_templates.title: Research and Save Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] with my documented tools, summarize the findings, then request approval before saving them to [destination].
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a reusable multi-tool sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable workflow for [goal] using my available Zapier tools. Compare MCP orchestration with existing Zaps and include approval and failure handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user is evaluating a complex automation pattern.

output_examples.input: Which workflow should handle my daily research digest?
output_examples.output: The documented Daily AI Digest is the closest match. It gathers research and delivers a report, but it has not been triggered.

output_examples.input: Track a 42 dollar software expense in my preferred sheet.
output: Planned fields: amount 42 dollars, category software, date pending

output_examples.input: Create a repeatable competitor research process.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: research each competitor, summarize comparable facts, review the results, then save approved findings to the selected sheet.

best_practices: Review the target, inputs, costs, and external effects before approving any automation.
Keep webhook credentials outside skill files and rotate any URL that was exposed.
Use precise trigger phrases and verify connected tool permissions regularly.
anti_patterns: Do not trigger workflows from ambiguous requests or broad words such as run.
Do not store real webhook URLs in repositories or shared skill files.
Do not persist conversational instructions without validation and explicit approval.

faq.question: Does this skill require Zapier MCP?
faq.answer: No. It can use webhook-triggered Zaps, connected MCP tools, or both.

faq.question: Can it create a Zap in the Zapier dashboard?
faq.answer: It provides setup guidance, but dashboard creation depends on available browser or Zapier tools and user permissions.

faq.question: How are workflow preferences remembered?
faq.answer: Approved tool preferences and patterns are written to the skill reference files for later sessions.

faq.question: Are webhook URLs safe to store in the skill?
faq.answer: No. Webhook URLs can authorize Zap execution and should be stored through an approved secret-management method.

faq.question: Will it run a workflow automatically?
faq.answer: The source workflow supports direct execution. Marketplace users should require explicit approval before any external side effect.

faq.question: Which services can it coordinate?
faq.answer: It can coordinate configured Zapier actions, including documented examples for Perplexity, Google Sheets, email, and webhook-triggered Zaps.
